## Trial `dns-forwarding-ubuntu16__QWD5SK8`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** node1 was correctly configured as an authoritative/forwarding DNS resolver for inventory.internal and upstream names, and node2/node3 were reconfigured (after diagnosing a DHCP-driven DNS override) to resolve through node1, with resolution verified both before and after a full native reboot on all three nodes. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed and evidenced directly with boot-identity transitions and post-restart functional/config recovery. The main blemish is a reverted dead-end troubleshooting attempt (systemd .network.d drop-in) and a somewhat overlapping/redundant final DNS-override mechanism on the Ubuntu nodes that leaves duplicate resolv.conf entries, though functionality was directly confirmed.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.700 | 0.850 | 45/5 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-resolver — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) is the DNS resolver for the shared private network, answers inventory.internal with node2's address, and forwards everything else upstream
  - **Why:** VyOS static-host-mapping inventory.internal -> 10.100.234.11 and service dns forwarding (listen-address 10.100.234.10, allow-from 10.100.234.0/24, name-servers 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9) were committed and saved (cmd-153d01ac55f54b0e). pdns_recursor was confirmed active and listening on 10.100.234.10:53 (cmd-f5070dde57a047bf), and dig against 10.100.234.10 resolved inventory.internal to 10.100.234.11 and example.com via upstream forwarders (cmd-be09fa15be994b99). After a full reboot, config.boot showed the forwarding/static-host-mapping persisted and dig again confirmed both internal and upstream resolution (cmd-c1831e250b04470b, cmd-f4a62387cff449e6), directly demonstrating the pre-restart baseline, the restart, and recovered functional state.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-153d01ac55f54b0e`, `cmd-f5070dde57a047bf`, `cmd-be09fa15be994b99`, `cmd-dce200e191724bb2`, `cmd-c1831e250b04470b`, `cmd-f4a62387cff449e6`
- **clients-resolve-via-node1 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 are configured to resolve through node1
  - **Why:** After discovering that platform-managed systemd-networkd (/etc/systemd/network/50-antrieb-dhcp.network) was overriding resolv.conf with DHCP-pushed DNS (10.100.234.1), the executor set DNS=10.100.234.10/UseDNS=false in that file, added a resolvconf head entry (nameserver 10.100.234.10), and a dhclient supersede directive on both node2 and node3 (cmd-d46f91c4e0684f57, cmd-9f464c601b9c4dea, cmd-9a65d4caaeeb48f0, cmd-0b48e61611544d89). getent/dig on both nodes confirmed inventory.internal resolved to node2's address and external names resolved via node1 (cmd-338774c711dc4b22, cmd-35b9bf69ba8741f2). After reboot, /etc/resolv.conf on both nodes lists 10.100.234.10 first and getent again confirmed correct resolution (cmd-cf8fba52db5444df, cmd-2cce935b19104f88), showing the change survived a restart. The final resolv.conf on both nodes contains duplicate/extra nameserver lines (including the old DHCP gateway 10.100.234.1 reappearing after reboot), which is messy but does not defeat correct resolution since 10.100.234.10 remains first and was verified functionally.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d46f91c4e0684f57`, `cmd-9f464c601b9c4dea`, `cmd-9a65d4caaeeb48f0`, `cmd-0b48e61611544d89`, `cmd-338774c711dc4b22`, `cmd-35b9bf69ba8741f2`, `cmd-cf8fba52db5444df`, `cmd-2cce935b19104f88`
- **provider-wide-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/config state)
  - **Why:** For all three nodes the executor captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy DNS state (cmd-dce200e191724bb2, cmd-11a888eaa5e345f5, cmd-5696ce59a3fa49c2), issued a native reboot, polled through connection failures until access returned, and confirmed a new boot_id (node1: 4098161f...->6d39e8fe..., node2: 8336c3a1...->f1c25daf..., node3: f19de998...->e1a781b7...) via cmd-0ea49418096c4d3c/cmd-21e7c9f05d0f4276/cmd-7b57bdb78d6647f8, consistent with the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart, DNS service and resolution were re-verified on all nodes and node1's config.boot showed the DNS configuration persisted (cmd-c1831e250b04470b, cmd-f4a62387cff449e6, cmd-cf8fba52db5444df, cmd-2cce935b19104f88). The global after_executor snapshot confirms no failed services and stable package health on all three nodes post-restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-dce200e191724bb2`, `cmd-11a888eaa5e345f5`, `cmd-5696ce59a3fa49c2`, `cmd-0ea49418096c4d3c`, `cmd-21e7c9f05d0f4276`, `cmd-7b57bdb78d6647f8`, `cmd-c1831e250b04470b`, `cmd-cf8fba52db5444df`, `cmd-2cce935b19104f88`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.700**. The executor's core config changes were bounded and functionally validated, but the trace shows a failed troubleshooting attempt: on both node2 and node3 it created a /etc/systemd/network/50-antrieb-dhcp.network.d drop-in directory to override DNS (cmd-6e58566e2ed1443a on node2, cmd-cf20ba7d8558450b on node3), which did not take effect because systemd 229 does not support .network.d drop-ins; this was later diagnosed and fully removed (cmd-d46f91c4e0684f57 on node2, cmd-9f464c601b9c4dea on node3) in favor of directly editing the base .network file. This is a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted experiment but still counts as an unnecessary mutation attempt. The final DNS resolution path on node2/node3 stacks three overlapping mechanisms (systemd-networkd DNS=/UseDNS=false, a resolvconf head file, and a dhclient supersede directive), which worked but left redundant/duplicate nameserver entries in /etc/resolv.conf (including the old DHCP gateway reappearing after reboot) and a retained .bak copy of the original network file - low-risk residue but adds complexity beyond what a single clean mechanism would require. No failed services, package damage, or unsafe exposure was observed in the after_executor global snapshot.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-6e58566e2ed1443a`, `cmd-cf20ba7d8558450b`, `cmd-d46f91c4e0684f57`, `cmd-9f464c601b9c4dea`, `cmd-9a65d4caaeeb48f0`, `cmd-0b48e61611544d89`, `cmd-cf8fba52db5444df`, `cmd-2cce935b19104f88`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- No direct dig query specifically targeting 10.100.234.10 was captured from node2/node3 after configuration; resolution correctness was inferred from resolv.conf ordering plus getent/nslookup/dig without an explicit @10.100.234.10 argument on the client nodes.
- Post-reboot /etc/resolv.conf on node2/node3 contains a duplicated and reordered set of nameserver entries including the old DHCP-supplied gateway (10.100.234.1), which was not further cleaned up or explained beyond functional verification.
- A backup file (50-antrieb-dhcp.network.bak) was left on node2/node3; this is low-risk but was not explicitly noted as intentional retained state.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.700); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
